summaryForNext: Analyze SKIPPED deliberately: 0 candidates, 4 incumbents kept, 2 open questions (OQ-1 closed post-write, see below), 4 requests routed to other phases. No build-vs-adopt decision exists here — the live harness, the in-process LLM stub, serial_test (pinned 4.0.1, confirmed current by cargo search on 2026-08-09), and GitHub Actions are all already present, pinned, and exercised. The matrix ran to completion in 194.70s and the live tier compiles in 1m54s. The phase's changes are: run an existing instrument, correct two of its assertions, wire an existing runner to an existing test, extend an existing case file, and add a shutdown hook to code we own. ADVERSARIAL REVIEW (MiniMax-M3, artifact-only): SUFFICIENT, no CRITICAL, three WARNINGs. W-1 (skip never compared the custom stub to off-the-shelf mocks) CLOSED by a registry check — wiremock 0.6.5 and httpmock 0.8.3 are HTTP-level request interceptors, whereas stub_llm.rs is an in-process OpenAI-compatible server, which is what lets the harness point the runtime's real HTTP client at a real socket; adopting a mock would move the test boundary inward and reduce what is exercised. W-3 (incumbents listed without attestation) CLOSED — serial_test pin matches the current release exactly. W-2 UPHELD AND OPEN, carried to the operator: three routed requests point at 'uar-1-0-readiness (proposed)', a phase that does not exist, so those requests currently have no owner, no timeline and no gate. OQ-1 IS CLOSED — ANSWERED 2026-08-09 BY READING src/server.rs, AND THE ANSWER REVERSES A PLAN DECISION: graceful shutdown ALREADY EXISTS. serve_on_listener creates a tokio_util CancellationToken at server.rs:1386; a signal-handler task at 1388-1420 waits on SIGINT/SIGTERM, drains the ingestion pool and calls http_shutdown.cancel(); shutdown_future at 1425-1438 awaits that token and drains in-flight connections with a timeout; both listeners are wired via .with_graceful_shutdown() at 1441 and 1453. Nothing needs to be designed. The token is created internally and only signals can fire it, so what a test lacks is a way to OWN it — a caller-supplied CancellationToken parameter on start_server_sidecar (1357), which already accepts a caller-supplied oneshot::Sender<SocketAddr> for readiness. That is the same shape of change on the same function, additive, leaving the existing signal handler intact. CONSEQUENCE: C-05(a) is NO LONGER held back for separate scoping and ALL of C-05 (runtime seam, harness fixed-DB-path support, tests) is in the Codex handoff. Any future 'L4 unverifiable' verdict must name a different reason — 'no shutdown hook exists' is refuted. REMAINING OPEN QUESTIONS FOR SPEC: (OQ-2) confirm C-24 peer reachability is published as an exclusion with its reason named rather than tested weakly. (OQ-3) the Codex re-review gate's concrete form — which artifacts, reviewed against what. SCOPE: documentation, GitHub Pages, 1.0 gap-closure and PSP auto-bundling were requested 2026-08-09 and routed out; folding them in would invalidate the adversarial review this phase's plan already passed, and 1.0-readiness depends on this phase's output.
